content:
Hello everyone, I'm doing a Masters in Mathematics and working on a thesis around formalizing some polynomial quotient ring results in Lean/mathlib.

The core idea is to formalize the ideal structure of F[X]/(f), building toward the standard result that F[X]/(f) is a field iff f is irreducible. I know a chunk of this is probably already in mathlib somewhere, so I'm trying to figure out where the actual gaps are rather than re-proving stuff that's already there.

Would appreciate some input from people who know the library better than I do:

  • Is this a sensible scope for an MSc thesis, or am I over/underestimating it?
  • What's already well-covered in this area, and where do the useful gaps seem to be?
  • If I want this to produce a real mathlib contribution (not just a personal formalization), how should I be approaching that?
  • Any specific files or existing formalizations worth studying first?
  • Anything you wish someone had told you before your first algebra formalization in Lean?

Still pretty new to Lean/mathlib, so any pointers at all are welcome. Thanks!

Welcome!

Rongsenchiten Jamir said:

building toward the standard result that F[X]/(f) is a field iff f is irreducible. I know a chunk of this is probably already in mathlib somewhere, so I'm trying to figure out where the actual gaps are rather than re-proving stuff that's already there.

#42333 proves this. Perhaps you could join the conversation at #Is there code for X? > `AdjoinRoot` is a field?

Rongsenchiten Jamir said:

If I want this to produce a real mathlib contribution (not just a personal formalization), how should I be approaching that?

Small PRs, and open your first one ASAP. Working on a big project privately and PRing everything when it's finished is not great, unless you have to work this way since it's a thesis.

Thanks for pointing me to #42333! I'll take a closer look at that proof and at the existing AdjoinRoot API.

My thesis idea is broader than just the field criterion. I was particularly interested in understanding/formalizing the ideal structure of polynomial quotient rings and the correspondence with divisors of the polynomial. So I'll investigate which parts of that development are already available and where there might be gaps.

Also, thanks for the advice about starting with small PRs. Since I'm still quite new to Lean/mathlib, I think getting a small PR out early would be a good way to learn the contribution workflow.

Would it make sense for me to look for a small first PR around "Polynomial", "Ideal", "Ideal.Quotient", or "AdjoinRoot", particularly results connecting polynomial divisibility with ideals or quotients? If anyone knows of a small issue or missing lemma in this area that would be suitable for a first PR, I'd really appreciate a pointer.
